arm6_midlowLR_cpt.what_a_proper_design_needs: NOT more dose points. (1) >=3 seeds per LR band with the DistributedSampler seed= fix ce5c298 actually in effect -- this repo's prior 'seed variance' arms were init-variance only; (2) a null arm = same data, same LR, same steps, run TWICE, to establish the run-to-run floor every arm difference must clear (nothing here has this); (3) average over a checkpoint window, not a single step; (4) pre-register the dose point before seeing the trajectory, or report trajectory-mean with a trajectory-level CI. Cost ~9 runs x 11.4h on 8xH20 ~= 4.3 node-days. Given the best effect estimate is +0.088pp, the honest prior is that there is nothing to find.

phase_locked_defect.mechanism: tcodex + MAIN verified .73:train_olmo2_arch_probe2.py:863 = DistributedSampler(ds, shuffle=True) with NO seed= (ce5c298 fix exists on wzc1, never scp'd to zwfy6). All three arms consumed the IDENTICAL minibatch sequence; training-loss corr Arm3-Arm6 = 0.99982.
phase_locked_defect.reading: The oscillation is a DETERMINISTIC function of data order, not noise -- and all three arms share that data order. So 'Arm 6 replicates Arm 3' reduces to 'the same data prefix produces the same effect at the same step', which it must. Arm 4 is the sole divergent arm at step220 and is precisely the arm whose data path is known-broken (redo from step215 without dataloader offset; original-vs-redo loss r = -0.0667). Most parsimonious account: data order determines the trajectory; the one arm that diverges is the one whose data order changed. LR is NOT demonstrated to be the causal variable.

what_is_established: At step220000 on this fixed data order, both low-LR arms show triviaqa em ~+0.5pp SIG with contains and f1 also SIG positive. A real, reproducible-under-identical-data effect, not a single-run fluke.
Arm 3's headline is not 'argmax of an oscillating series' in the sense my step215 verdict claimed -- an adjacent LR band lands on the same value at the same step.
what_is_NOT_established: That LR is the causal variable. Arm3 (0.249x) and Arm6 (0.425x) differ 1.7x in LR yet land within 0.02pp. Varying LR across arms while holding data order fixed cannot separate LR effect from data-order effect at this step.
That the effect generalizes past this data order. ZERO data-order replication exists.
That the trajectory shape means anything -- the step210 spike and step215 null are shared across arms at r~0.99, i.e. properties of the data stream at those steps.
Arm 4's 'peak-LR harms' -- still retracted, data-path-broken. Banner on ARM4_PEAKLR_VERDICT.md stands.

ckpt_corruption_incident_20260810.root_cause: BOTH watchers used a ready-test that a partially-written file passes. torch.save creates the file and then streams 12.18 GB into it. Trainer-side (scripts/_run_a03_arm4_peaklr.sh) used bare `[ -f ]` -> fired 8s after the step line, SIGTERM + sleep 20 + kill -9 at +28s; a 12.18 GB save cannot finish in 28 s on this FS. Eval-side (.82) used mtime age >= 120s, which cannot distinguish 'finished' from 'SIGKILLed mid-write so mtime froze'.

Luck, not design -- without that coincidence the headline 20k dose-point would have been computed from a 49% checkpoint.
